alternates.summary: Factories built to supply America’s electric-vehicle boom are getting a second life making batteries for the power grid. As EV demand weakens and electricity demand from data centers and new factories strengthens, battery makers are shifting toward stationary storage, but the new market still relies on federal incentives and a supply chain that remains partly dependent on China. The shift is visible at TransGrid’s Atlas projects in Arizona, where the contractor Qcells is using LG Energy Solution’s US-made battery cells. (Source: Bloomberg)
alternates.title: The EV Bust Creating a New Battery Boom

alternates.summary: The OpenAI software engineer charged with using a hidden recording device in one of the company’s offices asked to be freed from custody and denied his purchase of a one-way plane ticket to his native Saudi Arabia was part of a plan to flee US justice.
alternates.title: Arrested OpenAI Engineer Seeks Bail, Denies Planning to Flee

articles.summary: Over the weekend, Masad clarified that OpenAI would replace Anthropic as its default model provider. Claude will still be available to customers on the platform.
articles.title: Replit makes OpenAI its default over Anthropic, CEO says

articles.summary: The composition of Anthropic’s workforce and the type of work getting done have changed significantly in the past year.
articles.title: Anthropic says its workforce has become less junior and is spending more time in meetings

articles.summary: DeepSeek released an update of its AI model this weekend that it says is faster and leaner, ramping up the Chinese company’s challenge to Silicon Valley rivals Anthropic PBC and OpenAI as well as domestic competitors like Moonshot Kimi and Z.ai
articles.title: DeepSeek Pushes Out Updated AI Model It Says Is Faster, Leaner

articles.summary: A Meta spokesperson insisted that the updated terms did not reflect a change in the way Meta crawls the web.
articles.title: Meta removes language that raised scraping and AI training concerns

articles.summary: Autonomous agents are the hottest thing in AI. OpenAI, Meta, Google, Instinct, and others promise their agents can scour the internet on your behalf, doing anything from booking a dinner reservation and cleaning out your inbox to buying new shoes. But what happens when the rest of the internet won't play nice? In recent weeks, […]
articles.title: Websites are closing their doors to AI agents

articles.summary: After backlash, Meta is updating its terms again to remove language that suggested it could scrape content from sites, including news sites, to train its AI. Specifically, the following language no longer appears on the commercial terms page: … Meta may use any content from such domains, web pages, or URLs to provide, develop, improve, […]
articles.title: Meta removes language that may have allowed it to scrape news sites

articles.summary: Ritholtz Wealth Management Chairman and Chief Investment Officer Barry Ritholtz tells Bloomberg This Weekend that AI remains a transformational technology, but investors face a difficult task determining which companies will ultimately emerge as winners and losers. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Ritholtz discusses CoreWeave’s selloff, concerns about AI financing and valuations, and the challenges facing Tesla as competition in electric vehicles intensifies. (Source: Bloomberg)
articles.title: AI Selloff Tests Investor Confidence

articles.summary: Restrictions on Ukraine’s military use of SpaceX’s Starlink system appear to be deliberate and not the result of any technical problems, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, while denouncing a US decision to waive sanctions against Russia.
articles.title: Zelenskyy Says Starlink Speed Restrictions Look Deliberate
